content:
alex: FYI I ran a profiling sweep after the kernel-router tweak — seeing higher kernel-fallbacks when FP8/quantized KV is enabled and long prefixes are common. p99/token latency up ~10% for Mixtral under mixed batch shapes.

maria: can you drop the flamegraph link and a short diff of the router heuristics? want to confirm it's kernel selection, not batching.

alex: pasted traces: https://pprof.internal/runs/1822400011/flame.html — quick summary: increased calls into fallback_matmul and frequent small reallocs on kv-slab during prefix reinserts. attention kernel itself unchanged.

sahil: sounds like packing/alignment causing preferred-kernel stride mismatch. do we have a reproduction with varying head_dim / rope_scale?

alex: yes. repro script: perf/scripts/kv_align_repro.sh (ran against Llama-30b / Mistral-7b / Qwen-2.7b) showed correlation between head_dim % simd_width and fallback_rate. RoPE scaling shifts token shapes so the cache slab offsets vary more.

jen: interesting. so two levers: (1) make kernel-router aware of kv.format==FP8 and prefer kernels with tolerant strides, or (2) change kv-packing to maintain consistent stride at cost of some padding. Both have tradeoffs.

maria: don't blindly prefer one kernel across the fleet. let's design a canary: route a slice to a router variant that prefers fp8-tolerant kernels when kv.quantized=true and another slice that uses fixed-stride packing (pad to alignment). instrument a few counters.

alex: implemented both variants in canary branch:
```
# kernel-router v2 pseudo-config
if kv.format == FP8:
  if kv.packing == "unaligned": prefer fp8_tolerant_kernel
  else prefer fast_fp8_kernel
```
and packing patch pads to 64B boundary.

ci-bot: Deploy started: canary 15% nodes - r-2026.3.19-fp8-kv-canary

perf-bot: scheduled job perf/kv-align/1822400011 against reprompt shapes (short/long/prefix-heavy)

alex: early canary numbers (2 hours):
- kernel_fallback_rate: baseline 0.28 -> router-v2 0.09, pack-pad 0.06
- mixtral p99 token-latency: baseline 210ms -> v2 190ms, pack-pad 185ms
- qwen p99 token-latency: baseline 240ms -> v2 215ms, pack-pad 210ms
- shard memory usage: baseline 6.4GB -> v2 6.6GB, pack-pad 6.9GB (padding overhead)

maria: pack-pad reduces fallbacks more but increases memory. v2 is middle ground. any change in eviction churn?

alex: eviction_rate drops ~40% for v2, ~55% for pack-pad. interestingly pack-pad reduced read amplification for long streaming prefixes.

sahil: what about micro-batching behavior? earlier we saw eviction churn when micro-batches split long-prefix requests. maybe tweak batch-fill to prefer coalescing requests with matching prefix_affinity.

jen: propose adding a lightweight hint header 'x-prefix-affinity: <key>' so scheduler can try to keep those on same shard for short window. low-risk and reversible.

maria: agree. add a TTL for affinity (e.g., 1s) to avoid hotspotting. instrument affinity_miss_rate.

alex: added hint and micro-batching change. canary update: affinity hit-rate ~72% in the traffic slice, p99 tokens improved another ~3-4%. fallback_rate dips slightly more.

sahil: good. now for model-specific tuning: Mistral needs a different simd_threshold in kernel selection because head_dim small, while Llama benefits from pad-based approach for head_dim multiples. we should keep config per-model family.

maria: create table for per-model heuristics and default fallback thresholds. also add a metric stride_misalignment_count and kv_reinsert_count per-request.

alex: created perf job perf/jobs/kv-prefetch/1822400011 that runs overnight. scripts push results to perf-dashboard: dashboards/kv-align/1822400011.

jen: notes for release:
- roll forward: enable router-v2 by default for fp8 quantized KV after 48h stable canary.
- alternative: enable pack-pad only for models with head_dim mod simd in problematic set (table attached in the ticket).
- rollout risks: memory increase due to padding, possible cold-start tail for very small batches (we saw +2% for tiny micro-batches). rollback plan: revert router flag first, then packing pad.

maria: please add the changelog blurb and an ops playbook entry with the rollback commands and metric thresholds to auto-trigger rollback.

alex: added CHANGELOG.md entry and ops/runbook/rollback-kv-fp8.sh on the deploy page. CI job for canary monitors: stride_misalignment_count > 0.05 per-req and fallback_rate > 0.15 will auto-alert.

perf-bot: overnight run complete. summary:
- overall p99 tokens: Mixtral -6.8%, Mistral -5.2%, Qwen -5.9% (v2 + prefix affinity + selective padding)
- memory per-shard: +2.8% average, but active eviction decreased 48% -> net active working set smaller
- fallback_rate: -64%

jen: solid. next experiments:
1) tiered eviction policy (LRU for small prefix keys; MRU for streaming prefixes) to reduce reinsert cost.
2) microbench kernel latency for fp8_tolerant_kernel on cold vs warm caches to ensure no unexpected slowdown.
3) verify telemetry for enterprise private deployments (VPC) where memory tradeoff might be unacceptable.

sahil: I'll own (1). alex will run (2). maria to validate (3) with product/security.

alex: thanks all. I'll leave the canary running for the rest of the day and open a follow-up RFC for per-model router heuristics. :thumbsup:
